name: One Hour Turkey
brief_description: For Chef John's one-hour turkey recipe, you'll learn how to roast a whole turkey—yes, a whole turkey—in an hour. The secret is spatchcocking, a technique that reduces roasting time, preserves the succulent, moist breast meat, and also, the word is just fun to say.

instructions.text: Remove wing tips and tail section from turkey if desired, and reserve for stock.

To spatchcock, place turkey, breast side down, on a work surface. Starting at the tailbone, cut along either side of the backbone with scissors or a knife, cutting as close to the bone as possible. Reserve backbone for stock or discard.
Cut through any meat holding onto the shoulder blades to expose them, pull shoulder blades out to dislocate from the shoulder joint, and pull or cut to remove them.
Make a small cut into the cartilage right at the tip of the breastbone. Grasp the turkey ribcage on both sides and bend down until turkey flattens.
Once spatchcocked, season the underside evenly with half the salt and the black pepper. Turn the bird over; season the skin side evenly with remaining salt. Refrigerate until ready to roast.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C) and place an oven rack in the upper center.
Lay a large piece of heavy-duty aluminum foil over a standard 13x18-inch sheet pan, large enough to leave 4 or 5 inches of foil beyond the edges of the pan. Place a baking rack on top.

Center the turkey skin side up on the rack. Additional pieces of foil can be placed between the rack and the sheet pan if the ends of the wings and legs are sticking over the edge. Crimp foil upward to send any drips back into the pan.

Roast turkey in the preheated oven for about 1 hour. An instant read thermometer should read 150 to 155 degrees F (66 to 68 degrees C) inserted in the center of the thigh. Let rest at least for 15 minutes before serving.
